Tonight's d-11 fix re-derived --fg-disabled from --foreground and measured a worst case of 5.25:1 light / 5.27:1 dark across every preset that existed when it ran. womens-fashion did not exist then, and on its stand the disabled 'Select variant' button measures rgb(90,87,80) on rgb(140,59,46) = 1.04:1 at both viewports in both modes — worse than the 2.07:1 the fix was written to cure. So the disabled pair is not preset-independent: a preset whose --bg-disabled leans chromatic can defeat a foreground derived from --foreground. Two ways: derive --fg-disabled per preset with a contrast target rather than a fixed percentage, or constrain what a preset may put in --bg-disabled. The second is cheaper and narrows what a theme may express; the first is the honest fix. Which — and should the remaining themes wait for it?

A foundation defect that belongs to the wave, found by home-goods and confirmed to affect electronics too: the full-bleed hero's subheadline computes to rgb(36,28,22) — that is --foreground, dark ink on a dark photograph — because Tailwind's /80 opacity modifier cannot compose against --contrast-fg-primary, which is already rgba(255,255,255,.88) and is one of the 31 open bridge rows. Every full-bleed profile carries it and no edit to a hero can fix it. Either --contrast-fg-primary stops carrying its own alpha (so modifiers can compose), or full-bleed heroes stop using an opacity modifier and get an explicit second token for the subheadline. The first is one bridge row and touches every surface using that token; the second is a component change and touches only heroes. Which?
